subject: RStan Getting Started Guide: minor suggestion to speed up compilation speed

messages.author: 1718a05954397331
messages.subject: RStan Getting Started Guide: minor suggestion to speed up compilation speed
parts:
Dear Stanisticians,

The RStan Getting Started Guide (https://code.google.com/p/stan/wiki/RStanGettingStarted) suggests bumping up compiler optimization level to -O3, by changing the line:

 CXXFLAGS = -g -O2 $(LTO)

but makes no mention of removing the -g flag (which includes debugging information in the compiled object code).  For normal Stan users, is there actually a purpose to keeping the debug info at all?

If I remove the -g, I consistently get about 20% faster compiles on my system (Mac OS X 10.6). I have not tested on other platforms, but I surmise that a suggested installation procedure should nudge the user towards the fastest default.

What's been the experience of others?

    + Nicolas

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: RStan Getting Started Guide: minor suggestion to speed up compilation speed
parts:
Once RStan is installed, it is better to use

set_cppo("fast") # -O3 and no -g

or

set_cppo("debug") # -O0 -g and -DNDEBUG

if you have a runtime error.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] RStan Getting Started Guide: minor suggestion to speed up compilation speed

The installation of RStan uses O3 and it is configured within the package if it is not overwritten by Mafevar file in folder .R under the user home directory.  So I think we can replace that part with using set_cppo() now.  Set_cppo was added after Stan 1.0.0.

--
Jiqiang
